messages.subject: Performance issue in Mac
parts:
Hi Henrik:

I am processing 142 arrays (250k StyI only) on a Mac Pro (two 3 GHz
dual core processors and 4Gb RAM). I am using the standard steps.
After 5 hours it has completed allelic cross talk calibration and is
currently doing RmaCnPlm. My question is not about the time taken but
rather that the other programs (firefox, thunderbird etc.) become
unresponsive very frequently. I am not running any other CPU/RAM
intensive programs. I can't switch between programs and often get the
rainbow colored wheel going round and round. I am using a local disk.
Activity monitor reports that there is little free memory but there is
over 1Gb inactive memory; the VM size is over 13Gb and the disk
activity is high. Maybe swapping like crazy?

Is there any way I can get other programs to be responsive on this
computer?

Thanks,
Venkat

I don't know the specifics of Mac/OSX, but on Windows I've noticed
that R never returns any of the memory it allocates to the OS. The
memory is only returned when the R process quits. This is a problem
is the memory is fragmented and R needs to allocate a large chunk;
then the fragmented memory it has can't be used and additional memory
is requested from the OS. I think this is the case on Windows, but
maybe/hopefully this is solved in OSX. Thus, I occasionally restart
my R sessions to return memory. You can safely do so as well, because
aroma.affymetrix will detect what is already processed and skip that.
That might help you with you immediate problem.

Check with 'top' to see how much memory the R session uses. The 250K
arrays shouldn't consume too much memory and it should be rather
constant over time/number of arrays. If it does, let me know. There
might be some cached results in some of the objects that are not
cleaned output properly.

R is single-threaded so, unless you have compiled R specially, I think
it will only utilize one of your two cores. Then the other processes
should be able to run on the free core. Is that what your system
monitor reports too?

So, my best suggestion for now is to restart the R session.

/Henrik

messages.author: 41ed89aa70b5d27c
messages.subject: Re: Performance issue in Mac
parts:
While R is single-threaded, on Mac OS X R links to Altivec which is a
multi-threaded BLAS. In order words: as soon as you do matrix algebra
you will utilize all of your cores. This is in general great, because
it speeds up the computations a lot (it is _really_ significant).
Unfortunately, it also implies that your computer can slow down if you
do big matrix computations. I do not know how to disable this, aside
from recompiling R (and an associated slowdown).

Kasper

messages.subject: Re: Performance issue in Mac
parts:
Ok, I thought a bit more.

You can use "renice" on the command line to change the "nice" setting
of R, that should make your system way more responsive. There are a
few GUIs available, like Benicer, Renicer and Process Wizard (I have
not tried any of them).

Basically nice tells the system the priority of a program. Low values
is high priority, so if you change R to say 10 or higher it should
work. See also man nice and man renice

On the command line you can see the nice setting of the programs by
# ps xl
(lookf or column NI)

The only question is how this work when R calls Altivec, I am not an
expert on how nice is inherited.

Kasper

messages.author: 67dd8164f9bfa181
messages.subject: Re: Performance issue in Mac
parts:
I have no real performance issues running up to 70x250k arrays,
sometimes in 3 parallel analyses, on an 8 core Mac Pro (8GB RAM,
Leopard Server). Main bottleneck is HD read/write, which is alleviated
by using a RAID array (and having the system on a separate WD
Raptor ...).

But no general "system slowdown", as one gets sometimes while loading
Parallels etc.

Michael.
